title: Self-Supervised, Physics-Driven Sparse-Array XACT Reconstruction Using Sinusoidal Implicit Neural Representation.
abstract: X-ray induced acoustic computed tomography (XACT) enables high-contrast bone imaging but typically relies on dense and expensive transducer arrays. Sparse array sampling introduces severe streak artifacts and loss of fine structural details in conventional reconstruction. This work aims to establish a robust reconstruction framework that achieves high-fidelity structural imaging under sparse sampling, thereby overcoming hardware density limitations and facilitating low-cost, high-resolution skeletal health assessment. We propose a self-supervised, physics-driven framework based on sinusoidal implicit neural representation. The unknown initial pressure distribution is parameterized as a continuous coordinate-to-pressure function via a sinusoidal representation network, and is coupled end-to-end with a differentiable acoustic forward simulator implemented in j‑Wave. Network optimization is performed by minimizing waveform residuals between measured and predicted signals, eliminating the need for paired ground-truth data. To improve training stability and accelerate convergence, an adjoint-based warm start and total variation regularization are employed. In experiments on simulated hand and femoral bone sparse array datasets, the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches under various sparse sampling conditions. Notably, for an osteoporotic femur imaged with only 64 transducer elements, the method effectively suppresses artifacts and faithfully preserves fine trabecular structures, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.43 dB and a root mean square error of 0.0239, surpassing the structural and quantitative accuracy of traditional reconstruction using a full 256‑element array. These results demonstrate that the framework supports stable XACT reconstruction under sparse array conditions and, with its favorable artifact suppression and microstructural preservation capabilities, offers a practical computational pathway toward low-cost, high-quality XACT imaging.

title: A transparent gel pad bolus enabling direct skin recognition in surface-guided radiation therapy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of repurposing a transparent ultrasound gel pad as a radiotherapy bolus, we focused on dosimetric performance and compatibility with surface-guided radiation therapy (SGRT). Methods A gel pad bolus composed of tamarind seed gum and polyhydric alcohols was compared with a conventional gel bolus and a thermoplastic bolus. Percent depth dose was measured for 6 MV and 10 MV photon beams and 6 MeV and 9 MeV electron beams. Straight-line optical transmittance was assessed over 380-830 nm. Surface recognition accuracy was quantified using the AlignRT SGRT system on a breast phantom. Results The gel pad produced a measurable bolus effect for both photon and electron beams, although superficial dose enhancement was lower than that of conventional materials (85.5% vs 90.3-91.5% at 6 MV). Deep doses beyond dmax agreed within 1% for photon beams. At 730 nm, the gel pad bolus demonstrated high transmittance (92.3%), compared with the gel (19.8%) and HM (36.6%) boluses. The SGRT recognition rate with the gel pad bolus (89.10%) was comparable to the no-bolus condition (92.93%, p = 0.13), whereas conventional boluses significantly reduced recognition (p < 0.001). Conclusions The transparent gel pad bolus enabled direct SGRT-based recognition of the underlying skin surface while maintaining clinically relevant bolus functionality. Advances in knowledge Optical transparency enables SGRT monitoring through a bolus, highlighting optical compatibility as an important design consideration.

title: Endoscopic and histologic healing distribution and persistent rectosigmoiditis in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Background Mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis (UC) is believed to follow a proximal-to-distal pattern. We evaluated colonic healing distribution in patients with moderate-to-severe UC receiving adalimumab. Methods Patients from the SERENE UC (Study of a Novel Approach to Induction and Maintenance Dosing with Adalimumab in Patients with Moderate to Severe Ulcerative Colitis) trial with full colonoscopies and segmental biopsies at screening, weeks 8, and 52 were included for endoscopic and histologic analyses if baseline Mayo endoscopic subscore (MES) or Robarts Histopathology Index (RHI) score, respectively, was >0 in the ascending, transverse, and/or descending colon. Data were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures to account for clustering of segments within a patient. Results Endoscopic and histologic analyses comprised 76 and 79 patients, respectively. Score reductions were significantly greater vs the rectum in the ascending (week 8: MES, mean -0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI), -1.03 to -0.52]; RHI, mean -4.70 [95% CI, -6.92 to -2.49]; week 52: MES, mean -0.63 [95% CI, -0.91 to -0.35]; RHI, mean -2.39 [95% CI, -4.64 to -0.15]), transverse (week 8: MES, mean -0.69 [95% CI, -0.94 to -0.43]; RHI, mean -3.57 [95% CI, -5.62 to -1.51]; week 52: MES, mean -0.64 [95% CI, -0.89 to -0.38]; RHI, mean -2.88 [95% CI, -4.99 to -0.77]), and descending colon (week 8: MES, mean -0.40 [95% CI, -0.67 to -0.13]; RHI, mean -2.55 [95% CI, -4.94 to -0.16]; week 52: MES, mean -0.52 [95% CI, -0.70 to -0.34]; RHI, mean -3.47 [95% CI, -5.37 to -1.56]). Endoscopic improvement/remission and histologic remission were significantly more likely in the ascending and transverse colon than the rectum. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.

title: Benchmark Evaluation of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Mammography: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: Objective To compare the diagnostic performance of five contemporary vision-enabled large language models (LLMs) in mammography interpretation using a case-control benchmark design. Methods A total of 200 cases were analyzed using a quota-balanced case-control design (100 malignant, BI-RADS 4-5; 100 controls, BI-RADS 1-2). All models (ChatGPT-5T, ChatGPT-5I, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) received standard mammography images. Models were evaluated for lesion detection, laterality, quadrant localization, lesion type, and malignant-benign discrimination. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, Cohen's κ, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Breast density was recorded for all cases, while histopathological subtype and lesion size were documented for malignant cases. Results Lesion detection accuracy ranged from 79% to 91%, with high malignant sensitivity (92%-100%) but lower specificity in normal cases (24%-82%). ChatGPT-5T performed best in laterality (83%; κ = 0.70) and quadrant localization (73%; κ = 0.62). Lesion type classification was modest (74%-85%). In malignant-benign discrimination, ChatGPT-5T achieved the highest balanced accuracy (87%), while ChatGPT-4o showed poor specificity (28%). The study cohort was predominantly composed of lower-density breasts, larger lesions, and invasive ductal carcinoma as the most common subtype. Conclusion Vision-enabled LLMs demonstrated high sensitivity for breast lesion detection and classification tasks. More deliberative models, particularly ChatGPT-5T, consistently outperformed faster counterparts, especially in spatial reasoning tasks. However, reduced specificity in normal cases underscores that current LLM outputs should remain under radiologist supervision as supportive second-reader tools rather than standalone diagnostic systems. Given the quota-balanced design and cohort composition, results should be interpreted as comparative benchmarking rather than real-world diagnostic performance.

title: Foundation models for cancer: advancing diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response-an NCI workshop report.
abstract: From March 24-26, 2026, the National Cancer Institute convened the Foundation Models for Cancer Workshop, bringing together more than thirty speakers from academia, government, and industry and attracting more than 2,000 registrants worldwide. The workshop examined the current state and future potential of foundation models and related artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in oncology. Presentations spanned single-cell biology, computational pathology, medical imaging, electronic health records, drug discovery, federated learning, and clinical decision support. Several themes emerged across the three-day meeting. First, the development of robust foundation models depends on access to high-quality, multimodal cancer datasets that are representative of the patient populations, disease stages, and clinical settings encountered in routine care. Second, prospective validation and evaluation in real-world clinical environments are essential for establishing the reliability, generalizability, and utility of AI-enabled tools. Third, while technical advances continue at a rapid pace, successful translation into cancer research and patient care will also require attention to implementation, workflow integration, interpretability, and data governance. Collectively, the workshop highlighted both the opportunities and challenges associated with applying foundation models to cancer research and clinical care and provided a forum for discussing future directions for the field.

title: The Ongoing Utility of Historical Military Photofluorographs-Tools to Identify Fallen US Soldiers From Past Wars as Cross-Validated by DNA and Dental Data in 180 Cases.
abstract: Introduction Mass chest X-ray formed a routine part of induction processes to the US armed forces in the 1940-1950s for tuberculosis screening. Today, the skeletal structure recorded in these medical miniature films serves to identify these same soldiers. In the US military's accounting/repatriation setting, chest radiograph comparisons have grown to be a primary identification mechanism alongside DNA and dental records. Identifications are now routinely conducted with contributions from miniature radiographic films. This article reviews the miniature radiographic film as an identification tool and provides the first evaluation of findings (180 cases) against gold standards of DNA and dental analyses for the very same cases. Materials and methods This article reviews both miniature film photofluorographs and the standardized chest radiograph comparison (CXR) protocol employed by the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) for identification. Additionally, all DPAA cases (2010-2025) where radiographic CXR resulted in a match result (280) were reviewed for additional DNA and/or dental record findings, providing 180 cases where dual-modality result existed to cross-validation test the radiographic analyses. Results For 172 DNA cases, there was no instance of disagreement between the chest radiograph result and the independently acquired Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory's DNA result. For 8 dental cases reporting a positive match result, the CXR identity finding was identical (both evidence lines identified the same person). To be conservative, we assume that the next future CXR case to be conducted using miniature films will yield an erroneous result, thereby setting a positive predictive value for radiographic comparison of 99.4% (=180 correct results/181 total decisions). Conclusions Miniature chest radiographs provide useful identification-relevant information. DPAA casework provides a rare circumstance to evaluate the accuracy of miniature film radiograph comparisons across a large sample, as multiple independent and parallel lines of analysis exist for single cases. Evaluation of these cases (180 in total) reveals that the military miniature films supply the same name associations that DNA and forensic odontology provide. The positive predictive value is high (99.4%), conservatively assuming the next case to be an incorrect one. This confirms the value of the miniature chest film and CXR methods, when DNA and dental records alone are unable to provide definitive answers.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema Score for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome-Post Hoc Analysis of the "Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis" Study.
abstract: Objectives To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and its interobserver reliability. Design Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study. Setting ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study. Patients Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days. Interventions None. Measurements and main results Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected for analysis. The primary outcome was ARDS according to the Berlin definition during the first 2 ICU days. Of 236 patients, 92 (39%) had ARDS. The median RALE score was higher in patients with ARDS than in those without (29.5 [22.2-34.5] vs. 12.2 [7.5-17.8]; p < 0.01). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.96). At the optimal cutoff of 20, sensitivity was 85%, specificity 83%, positive predictive value 76%, and negative predictive value 90%. Interobserver reliability was high, with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87. Conclusions In patients invasively ventilated for at least 2 days, the RALE score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

title: What Is the Validity of Traction MR Arthrography for Detecting Lesions of the Ligamentous-Fossa-Foveolar Complex in Patients Undergoing Joint-preserving Surgery Through Surgical Hip Dislocation?
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative characterization of intraarticular abnormalities is important when planning hip-preserving surgery in young, active patients. Lesions of the ligamentum teres and the associated acetabular fossa and fovea capitis (forming the ligamentous-fossa-foveolar complex [LFFC]) are frequently observed intraoperatively, although their relationship with hip pain in patients without osteoarthritis remains uncertain. These lesions have received limited attention in preoperative imaging. Questions/purposes (1) What is the intraobserver and interobserver reliability of traction MR arthrography for assessing lesions of the LFFC? (2) What is the diagnostic performance of traction MR arthrography for detecting these lesions compared with intraoperative findings at surgical hip dislocation? Methods Between April 2019 and April 2022, we retrospectively identified 214 hips from a consecutive cohort of patients undergoing surgical hip dislocation at a single tertiary hip preservation center. We performed this surgery for a variety of indications, including for symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement, childhood hip diseases, and for surgically treating acetabular fractures. During this period, preoperative MR arthrography was part of the routine preoperative work-up in all patients for assessment of intraarticular abnormalities, planning for intraoperative instrument and graft needs, and prognostic purposes. MR arthrography results were not considered when choosing surgical approach. Patients without traction MR arthrography were excluded. A total of 70 patients were available for final analysis. Traction MR arthrography served as the index test and intraoperative assessment during surgical hip dislocation as the reference gold standard. The decision to perform surgical hip dislocation was based on the clinical and standard radiographic evaluation and generally not influenced by traction MR arthrography findings. Six observers (three board-certified orthopaedic surgeons with expertise in hip-preserving surgery and three board-certified radiologists with specific expertise in musculoskeletal imaging) independently conducted measurements twice using an adapted version of a previously validated grading system (grade 0, normal; grade I, degeneration; grade II, partial defect; grade III, complete defect); for diagnostic performance, findings were dichotomized as lesion absent (grade 0) or present (grade > 0). Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) with 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated to assess intraobserver reliability and interobserver reproducibility of the adapted grading system. The diagnostic performance of traction MR arthrography for detecting lesions of the LFFC using intraoperative findings as a gold standard was determined by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, accuracy, and positive and negative likelihood ratios. Results Intraobserver reliability ICCs ranged from 0.54 to 0.69 for ligamentum teres lesions, 0.21 to 0.64 for fossa lesions, and 0.30 to 0.64 for fovea lesions. Interobserver reproducibility ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 for fossa lesions, 0.73 to 0.77 for fovea lesions, and 0.78 to 0.79 for ligamentum teres lesions. Traction MR arthrography demonstrated limited diagnostic performance for lesion detection. The sensitivity was 86% for ligamentum teres lesions, 79% for fossa lesions, and 75% for fovea lesions, whereas specificity was low at 32%, 52%, and 50%, respectively. Overall accuracy ranged from 54% to 67%. Conclusion In this cohort of patients undergoing surgical hip dislocation, contrast-enhanced traction MR arthrography demonstrated limited ability to detect and grade lesions of the LFFC preoperatively. Future prospective studies using standardized imaging protocols are needed to determine whether diagnostic performance can be improved. Level of evidence Level III, diagnostic study.

title: Group A Streptococcus in an Unexpected Site: Temporal Pyomyositis in 2 Children.
abstract: Background Pyomyositis is an uncommon bacterial infection of skeletal muscle. Group A Streptococcus (GAS) accounts for a smaller proportion of pediatric cases, and temporal muscle involvement is exceptionally rare. Case description We report 2 previously healthy children, a 7-year-old boy and a 6-year-old girl, who presented with acute otitis media (AOM) and painful unilateral temporomandibular swelling. Computed tomography revealed AOM with temporal myositis, complicated by mastoiditis in the first case. Both were treated with intravenous antibiotics, and the first case required drainage and mastoidectomy, with full recovery. GAS was isolated in both cases. Conclusions GAS temporal pyomyositis should be considered in children presenting with AOM and painful temporal swelling. Imaging is crucial for diagnosis and assessment of disease extent. Surgical management should be individualized.

Both were treated with intravenous antibiotics, and the first case required drainage and mastoidectomy, with full recovery. GAS was isolated in both cases.

Conclusions

GAS temporal pyomyositis should be considered in children presenting with AOM and painful temporal swelling. Imaging is crucial for diagnosis and assessment of disease extent. Surgical management should be individualized.

title: Parasitic Infections of the Lacrimal System: A Major Review of Etiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management.
abstract: Purpose Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare and often under-recognized causes of lacrimal pathology. Their clinical presentation frequently mimics more common conditions such as chronic dacryocystitis, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in appropriate management. This study aims to systematically review the literature on parasitic infections of the lacrimal system and to characterize their etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, Emcare, and PubMed from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting parasitic infections involving the lacrimal apparatus were included. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, anatomical involvement, causative organisms, diagnostic methods, treatment, and outcomes were extracted. Due to heterogeneity and predominance of case reports and small series, a qualitative descriptive analysis was performed. Results A total of 44 studies comprising 172 cases were included. Rhinosporidium seeberi was the most frequently reported pathogen, accounting for 147 cases (85.5%), followed by Leishmania (8 cases, 4.7%) and Ascaris lumbricoides (7 cases, 4.1%). The lacrimal sac was the most commonly involved site. Clinical presentation was nonspecific, with epiphora and medial canthal swelling predominating. Diagnosis was most often established by histopathology following surgical intervention. Management varied by etiology, with surgical excision commonly used for rhinosporidiosis and mechanical extraction for helminthic infections. Outcomes were generally favorable, although recurrence was reported, particularly in R. seeberi infections. Conclusions Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare but clinically important, with diverse presentations and management approaches. Increased awareness is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Further studies with standardized reporting are needed to optimize management strategies.

title: Adaptive Control Point B-Spline Method for Improving Accuracy and Deformation Plausibility in Deep Learning Brain Registration.
abstract: Deformable brain image registration plays a crucial role in aligning and jointly analyzing multi-phase and multi-modal neuroimaging data. However, existing unsupervised deep learning-based registration methods typically predict dense displacement fields directly at the voxel level, which often leads to deformation noise and optimization difficulties due to redundant degrees of freedom. Furthermore, these methods are prone to topological distortions when noise or irrelevant information is present. To address these challenges, we propose a robust B-spline registration post-processing framework with adaptive control point density, which can be seamlessly integrated into mainstream registration architectures for brain analysis. Specifically, we design a Control Point Spacing Predictor (CPSPredictor) that adaptively adjusts the distribution density of control points based on the input images, enabling effective regulation of registration flexibility. By modeling displacements with sparse control points and generating continuous and smooth deformation fields via locally supported B-spline basis functions, the proposed method significantly suppresses folding artifacts and preserves anatomical consistency. Extensive experiments on multiple publicly available brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our approach can be seamlessly integrated into existing mainstream registration frameworks, significantly improving both registration accuracy and the physical plausibility of the transformation. For instance, on the IXI dataset, our method boosts the VoxelMorph baseline's DSC by 2.63% and reduces the number of folding points nearly 69-fold. The resulting registration outputs better align with clinical diagnostic requirements, highlighting the method's robustness and practical application potential.

title: ScanSeg: Policy-Guided Sequential Prompting for Dense Fine-Grained Ultrasound Segmentation.
abstract: Dense fine-grained segmentation on standardized ultrasound planes is clinically essential but remains challenging because multiple anatomical structures coexist under speckle noise, acoustic shadowing, weak boundaries, and partial visibility. Promptable foundation models can produce high-quality masks when queried, but they typically return one structure at a time and lack a mechanism to automatically decide what to segment next and where additional evidence is needed, making single-shot "auto" outputs brittle on complex planes. This paper introduces ScanSeg, a scan-inspired framework that formulates multi-structure ultrasound segmentation as sequential evidence accumulation via a small number of prompted calls. ScanSeg maintains a global per-pixel posterior over classes and iteratively issues prompts to a SAM predictor to obtain structure-specific mask observations with confidence scores. Each observation is fused into the posterior through a stable logit-space evidence accumulation rule, preserving global competition among structures. To enable efficient scanning, a lightweight proposal policy is learned to select the next target structure and prompt location conditioned on the current posterior and its uncertainty, trained by supervised imitation from step-wise oracle actions defined by posterior residuals. Experiments on dense abdominal and fetal cardiac ultrasound planes demonstrate that ScanSeg consistently outperforms both single-shot and prompted baselines, yielding more reliable fine-grained multi-structure segmentation and improving average Dice by up to 6.52 points on Abdomen and 4.94 points on A4C with only a few predictor calls.

title: Acute Perinatal Stroke Characteristics and Outcome in Southern Finland.
abstract: Aim Perinatal stroke can cause lifelong morbidities. Outcome prediction is important for parental guidance and follow-up. We studied characteristics of acute perinatal stroke in a Finnish cohort. Methods We performed a population-based study, identifying infants with acute neonatal cerebral ischemia or sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) in Southern Finland from 2010 to 2023. We analysed the incidence of stroke types, seizures, anti-seizure medication use, and outcomes. Results Altogether 88 infants (1 in 3101 live births) were diagnosed with acute perinatal stroke: 67% with arterial ischemic stroke (AIS), 22% with hemorrhagic stroke (HS) and 11% with CSVT. Seizures and anti-seizure medication use occurred in 78% of infants. Cranial ultrasound infrequently recognized AIS but usually noted haemorrhage. During follow-up, 34% of infants had no adverse outcome diagnosis. The most common outcome was cerebral palsy (CP, 35%). A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types. Conclusion The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

title: Gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine with and without aura: A multimodal MRI and JuSpace analysis.
abstract: Objective To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates. Background Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Results Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction. Conclusion Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: A fluorescent choline kinase alpha inhibitor for intraoperative molecular imaging during resection of canine NSCLC tumors.
abstract: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. A near-infrared fluorescent ChoKα-targeting imaging agent, JAS239 (λ ex , λ em : 745, 775 nanometers), was developed for intraoperative identification of tumors, their margins, and local metastases. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

title: Impact of different clarithromycin resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: Macrolides remained cornerstone of Mycobacterium abscessus treatment, but emerging resistance patterns compromised therapeutic efficacies. Clarithromycin resistance can manifest as either mutational or inducible, while the clinical impacts of different resistance mechanisms in M. abscessus pulmonary disease (MAB-PD) had been poorly characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study from 2011 to 2023 across four tertiary centers in Taiwan. Adults with clarithromycin-resistant MAB-PD were included and stratified by resistance type: mutational vs inducible. Outcomes included all-cause 3-year mortality, microbiological clearance, and radiographic progression. Among 108 enrolled patients, 16 (14.7%) had mutational resistance and the remaining 92 had inducible type. Isolates comprised 103 M. abscessus , three M. massiliense , and two M. bolletii . Mutational resistance was associated with significantly higher 3-year mortality (18.8% vs 4.3%, P = 0.03) and lower acid-fast smear conversion rates in treated patients (18.2% vs 67.6%, P = 0.004). Multivariable analysis identified mutational clarithromycin resistance as an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 5.21, 95% confidence interval 1.10-24.6, P = 0.04). Strains with mutational resistance demonstrated higher median minimal inhibitory concentrations to linezolid (24 vs 16 mg/L), cefoxitin (64 vs 32 mg/L), and amikacin (16 vs 8 mg/L). Mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD is associated with substantially worse clinical outcomes compared to inducible resistance, including higher mortality and poorer treatment responses. These findings suggested that more intensive treatment strategies might be needed for mutational clarithromycin resistance in MAB-PD. Importance Macrolide resistance critically undermines treatment outcomes in Mycobacterium abscessus lung disease, yet the prognostic impact of distinct resistance mechanisms has remained unclear. This multicenter study demonstrates that mutational clarithromycin resistance, although less common than inducible resistance, is associated with markedly higher mortality, poorer microbiological response, and broader multidrug resistance. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence that not all macrolide resistance is equivalent. Recognizing mutational resistance as a high-risk phenotype has important implications for risk stratification, prognostication, and treatment intensification, supporting a more personalized approach to managing MAB-LD in routine clinical practice.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Opportunistic Screening of Left Ventricular Dysfunction Screening Using Chest Radiographs.
abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate a deep learning model (DLLV) for identifying reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on chest radiographs (CXRs) and assess its potential as a prescreening tool for selective transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in health checkup populations. Materials and Methods Same-day CXR-TTE pairs obtained between January 2016 and September 2021 were retrospectively collected for model development. Counterfactual learning was applied to enhance model performance and interpretability. External testing included one tertiary referral center cohort and two health checkup cohorts. Discrimination was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and DLLV-based prescreening was evaluated by estimated TTE reduction and missed-case burden. Results The development dataset included 24,674 patients (32,135 CXR-TTE pairs); external cohorts included 5440, 28,034, and 6085 patients (53-62% male). DLLV achieved an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.88) for LVEF ≤ 40% in the tertiary referral cohort. In health checkup cohorts, AUCs were 0.92-0.97 for LVEF ≤ 40%, with AUPRCs of 0.04 in both cohorts, corresponding to 87-fold (95% CI: 16, 404) and 37-fold (95% CI: 3, 251) enrichment over baseline prevalence. Counterfactual reinforcement learning produced heatmaps with greater heart localization precision ( P < .001 for all) and higher AUC for LVEF < 50% ( P = .04). DLLV-based prescreening estimated TTE volume reductions up to 85% while identifying all 12 and 7 individuals with LVEF ≤ 40%. Conclusion DLLV identified reduced LVEF on CXRs across external test cohorts and showed potential as a prescreening tool for selective TTE in health checkup populations. ©RSNA, 2026.

title: Agentic Automation of BT-RADS Scoring Using an End-to-End System for Standardized Glioma Follow-up Assessment.
abstract: The Brain Tumor Reporting and Data System (BT-RADS) standardizes posttreatment MRI response assessment in patients with diffuse gliomas but requires complex integration of imaging trends, medication effects, and radiation timing. An end-to-end multiagent large language model and convolutional neural network system for automated BTRADS classification was developed and evaluated. Five hundred nine consecutive posttreatment glioma MRI examinations (March 2017-July 2021) from a single center were retrospectively evaluated. An extractor agent identified clinical variables from notes using gpt-oss (OpenAI, 20-billion parameters). A scorer agent applied BTRADS decision logic integrating these with quantitative volumetrics. System accuracy was compared against initial assessments, using expert annotation as the reference standard. Four hundred ninety-two examinations were evaluable. Overall system accuracy was 76.0% (374/492) versus 57.5% (283/492) for initial assessments, an absolute difference of +18.5 percentage points ( P < .001). Cohen kappa between the system and the reference standard was 0.71. The system achieved high sensitivity in context-dependent categories (BT-1b; 100%; BT-1a, 92.7%; BT-3a, 87.5%) and moderate sensitivity for threshold-dependent categories (BT-3c, 74.8%; BT-2, 69.2%; BT-4, 69.3%; BT-3b, 57.1%). The BT-4 positive predictive value was 92.9%. These results support further evaluation of this system as a clinical decision-support tool, with local open-weight inference preserving data privacy.

title: Systematic differences between ultrasound and MRI assessment of fetal ventricular width in cases of fetal mild ventriculomegaly: a cohort study.
abstract: Prenatal assessment of the lateral ventricles is essential for detecting and classifying fetal ventriculomegaly (VM). Although ultrasound (US) is the primary screening tool, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly used to complement diagnosis. However, discrepancies between US and MRI measurements, particularly in mild VM, may affect classification, counseling, and planning clinical management. The aim of the study is to compare US and MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles, evaluate the agreement between both methods, with particular focus on mild ventriculomegaly, and additionally assess the feasibility of deriving conversion formulas between both modalities. Methods This cohort study included 120 fetuses examined between 2011 and 2021 at a referral center: 75 with isolated mild VM and 45 controls. All underwent a standardized US assessment and fetal MRI. Ventricular width was measured twice for each modality; mean values were used for statistical comparison. Analysis included Wilcoxon tests, Friedman tests, Bland-Altman plots, Pearson's chi-square tests, Theil-Sen regression, and linear modeling. Results MRI systematically provided greater ventricular measurements than US. In the study group, the bias was 0.71mm for coronal MRI and 0.33mm for axial MRI. Agreement between methods was limited, with measurement discrepancies observed in 34% of cases (coronal) and 33.3% (axial). Combined analysis of both groups confirmed persistent measurement discrepancies, though the overall axial MRI bias decreased to 0.15mm. Theil-Sen modelling enabled the development of conversion formulas for both measurement planes. Conclusions MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles tend to be slightly higher than ultrasound measurements, particularly in the coronal plane. These systematic differences may change the VM classification and should be considered in clinical interpretation. Ultrasound demonstrated better measurement reproducibility. The obtained formulas may support improved cross-modality comparison in clinical practice.

title: Secondary metastasis resection after biomarker-stratified first-line treatment of metastatic colorectal carcinomaInterim analysis of the IVOPAK II study with a risk-benefit assessment of secondary metastatic resection.
abstract: Objective The IVOPAK II study (Interdisciplinary Care with Quality Control in Palliative Treatment of Colorectal Cancer) prospectively evaluated the risk (postoperative complications, mortality) and benefit (overall survival) of multimodal treatment with secondary metastasis resection for initially nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma. Patients and methods A total of 40 patients from 10 centers were enrolled. Patients with quintuple wildtype (K-RAS, N-RAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, ERBB2, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus cetuximab, while patients with RAS-mutation (K-RAS or N-RAS, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. CT scans were presented at two-month intervals to the interdisciplinary tumor board at the University Hospital Erlangen to assess potentially curative secondary metastatic resection. After a median follow-up of 32 months, outcomes of the multimodally (chemotherapy treatment plus metastasis resection) and the palliatively (only chemotherapy treatment) treated patients were compared. Results The rate of secondary metastasis resection was 45% (18/40). Overall survival was significantly longer in the multimodal treatment group compared to the palliative treatment group (median 61 vs. 22 months, p=0.002), this also applied to progression-free survival (median 39 vs. 11 months, p=0.018). Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 morbidity occurred in 28% (5/18) of patients, and 90-day mortality was 6% (1/18). Univariate analyses revealed a significant improvement in overall survival among patients with ECOG performance status 0, solitary metastatic site and multimodal treatment. In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor. Conclusion Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.

Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 morbidity occurred in 28% (5/18) of patients, and 90-day mortality was 6% (1/18). Univariate analyses revealed a significant improvement in overall survival among patients with ECOG performance status 0, solitary metastatic site and multimodal treatment. In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor.

Conclusion

Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.

title: Lactation Management in Patients With Cancer: An Evidence-Based Framework for Surgical Practice.
abstract: BackgroundThe coexistence of lactation and cancer care, termed oncolactation , is becoming increasingly common as childbearing is delayed and more women are diagnosed with malignancy during the reproductive years. However, evidence-based guidance regarding breastfeeding during oncologic evaluation and treatment remains fragmented, particularly for surgeons involved in multidisciplinary cancer care.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with a systematic literature search using PubMed/MEDLINE and professional society guidelines (American Society of Breast Surgeons (ASBrS), American College of Radiology (ACR), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®). Publications addressing surgical management, diagnostic imaging, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, and reproductive counseling in lactating patients with cancer were critically synthesized to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.ResultsMost diagnostic and surgical interventions-including mammography, breast MRI, computed tomography, image-guided biopsy, and general anesthesia-are compatible with continued breastfeeding when appropriate precautions are observed. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and most targeted or immunotherapeutic agents remain contraindicated because of insufficient safety data or potential infant toxicity. Radiation therapy generally precludes breastfeeding from the treated breast, but permits continued feeding from the contralateral breast. Emerging evidence also supports individualized counseling regarding fertility preservation, future pregnancy, and survivorship.ConclusionsOncolactation should be incorporated into routine surgical oncology practice. Most surgical and diagnostic procedures can be performed without interrupting breastfeeding, whereas systemic therapies require individualized pharmacologic assessment. Integration of evidence-based lactation guidance into multidisciplinary cancer care promotes safe, patient-centered decision-making while maintaining oncologic safety and supporting breastfeeding whenever feasible.

title: A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Velopharyngeal MRI in Children With Unexplained Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the utility of velopharyngeal MRI in contributing additional diagnostic information for patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) of unknown etiology.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary children's hospital.ParticipantsChildren with clinically significant VPI without a confirmed etiology.InterventionsStandardized perceptual speech assessment with nasometry, non-sedated MRI, and multidisciplinary review for treatment planning.Main Outcome MeasuresMRI-informed etiologic classification, anatomic and functional contributors to VPI, and management recommendations.ResultsAmong 89 children, six (6.7%) presented with clinically significant VPI of unknown etiology on routine examination. MRI identified occult submucous cleft palate or atypical levator veli palatini morphology in five (83.3%) and adenoid-supported VP closure in three (50%). Involution was expected to unmask increased pharyngeal depth in two (33.3%). MRI supported patient-specific recommendations for speech therapy, surgical interventions, and longitudinal monitoring.ConclusionsMRI provided clinically meaningful diagnostic information beyond routine examination and informed management decisions for children with VPI.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: Interventions to increase participation in lung cancer screening programmes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). Methods Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. Results Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. Conclusions Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

title: Geriatric respiratory medicine 2026: from artificial intelligence to personalised management of the multimorbid patient.
abstract: The profound demographic shift toward an ageing population has decisively moved the burden of chronic and acute lung diseases towards older adults, necessitating a transition from organ-centred models to integrated, multidimensional care. This review outlines a pragmatic framework for managing the complex interplay of immunosenescence, frailty and multimorbidity. In acute care, "pneumonia-associated sarcopenia" is identified as a critical driver of recurrent infections and functional decline, requiring a shift towards aspiration prevention and the aid of diagnostic tools such as lung ultrasound. The selection of noninvasive respiratory support, including high-flow nasal cannulas and noninvasive ventilation, must balance physiological efficacy with the risks of delirium and patient self-inflicted lung injury. Preventive strategies have evolved with the introduction of 20-valent pneumococcal and respiratory syncytial virus vaccines, alongside proactive screening for ɑ1-antitrypsin deficiency to enable precision interventions. Chronic disease management emphasises a "device-centric" inhalation therapy approach, tailoring delivery systems to impaired peak inspiratory flows and cognitive status rather than to pharmacology alone. The advent of biological therapies, particularly the use of dupilumab and mepolizumab in eosinophilic COPD, offers a transformative "steroid-sparing" effect, aiming for clinical stability and preserved independence. Finally, the integration of artificial intelligence as "augmented intelligence" and the "4Ms" multidisciplinary model (mentation, medication, mobility, morbidities) provide the necessary tools to navigate clinical complexity. This holistic strategy ensures that technological innovation remains anchored in patient-centred goals.

title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in 68 Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
abstract: Background PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations. Methodology This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

title: Müllerian-type high-grade serous carcinoma presenting exclusively with pleural lesions and no detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor: a case report.
abstract: Background Müllerian-type high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) most commonly originates from the fallopian tube, ovary, or peritoneum and usually presents with abdominopelvic disease. Thoracic presentation without a detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor is extremely rare and poses a diagnostic challenge. Case presentation We report the case of a 60-year-old woman who was referred to our hospital after pleural thickening was detected during a routine medical checkup. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed left pleural thickening with mild pleural effusion. Thoracoscopic pleural biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle-shaped cells with mild nuclear atypia, with scattered calcifications and osteocyte-like elements. Immunohistochemical staining showed positivity for PAX8, WT-1, AE1/AE3, CK7, p16, and p53, and negativity for calretinin, D2-40, TTF-1, and Napsin A, supporting a Müllerian-type HGSC. Diagnostic/staging laparoscopy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy revealed no macroscopic tumor or disseminated lesions. Both ovaries and fallopian tubes were carefully examined pathologically, with the fallopian tubes examined using the SEE-FIM protocol. No malignant lesion or serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) was identified. Peritoneal washing cytology was negative. p53 and Ki-67 immunohistochemistry of the tubo-ovarian specimens was not performed. Discussion The absence of a detectable abdominopelvic primary tumor after radiological, laparoscopic, and pathological evaluation suggests an extremely rare thoracic presentation of Müllerian-type HGSC. Both ovaries and fallopian tubes were carefully examined pathologically, including examination of the fallopian tubes using the SEE-FIM protocol, and no malignant lesion or STIC was identified. Nevertheless, an occult microscopic Müllerian primary cannot be completely excluded, particularly because p53 and Ki-67 immunohistochemistry of the tubo-ovarian specimens was not performed. Primary pleural Müllerian carcinoma, EOPPC, and Müllerian-type HGSC of undetermined primary origin therefore remain possible classifications. Müllerian-type HGSC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of pleural tumors in women, even when no abdominopelvic primary tumor is identified. Comprehensive radiological, laparoscopic, and pathological evaluation is important for determining the most appropriate classification. In the absence of an identified primary site, classification should remain cautious, and EOPPC should be regarded as a possible interpretation rather than a definitive diagnosis.

title: Leveraging Digital Histopathology to Build Capacity and Collaboration Toward the Diagnosis of Pediatric Solid Tumors in Mexico.
abstract: Purpose Pediatric pathology in Mexico remains limited by an uneven distribution of specialized training and constrained resources, which can affect the accuracy of pediatric malignancy diagnosis. This study aimed to evaluate national diagnostic capacity for common organ-based pediatric solid tumors-renal tumors, neuroblastic tumors, and hepatic neoplasms-through a retrospective hybrid central pathology review. A secondary objective was to identify targeted areas for capacity building and strengthen collaborative networking. Materials and methods A hybrid retrospective pathology review (2005-2023) was conducted across eight institutions that treat pediatric oncology patients. Eligible cases included off-therapy patients age 0-18 years diagnosed with renal, hepatic, or neuroblastic tumors. Paraffin blocks, slides, clinical data, and original pathology reports were submitted. Cases underwent conventional pathology review, digital slide scanning, and joint virtual evaluation. Final diagnoses were compared between original, conventional central pathology review, and digital review, and individualized feedback was provided to each institution. Results A total of 162 specimens were reviewed, including 584 original stained slides, 940 paraffin blocks, and 1,168 digitized slides. At least 54 online review sessions were conducted, and 24 virtual feedback sessions were held. Overall diagnostic concordance across original, central, and digital evaluations was 80% for renal tumors, 90.9% for neuroblastic tumors, and 92.1% for hepatic neoplasms. Common limitations included inconsistent/inadequate sampling and incomplete/erroneous subclassification and reporting. Conclusion Findings confirm strong baseline diagnostic capabilities for common pediatric solid tumors across participating Mexican centers, while highlighting specific gaps in sampling, reporting standardization, and access to ancillary testing. The project facilitated the creation of a pediatric pathology network, demonstrating that a hybrid centralized-digital review model can strengthen specialized pediatric pathology capacity in resource-limited settings.

title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort. Methods Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers. Results A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (B MCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10 -4 ) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI] indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI] proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p 's < 5.01 × 10 -6 ) and Simoa-Based pTau181 ( p < 4.51 × 10 -15 ) and neurofilament light chain ( p < 5.34 × 10 -7 ). Discussion Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

title: Duplicated Appendix With Mucocele Mimicking an Appendiceal Neoplasm in a 45-Year-Old Woman: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Appendiceal duplication is an extremely rare congenital anomaly, with an incidence of 0.004% to 0.009%. An association with an appendiceal mucocele is even rarer. It can complicate the diagnosis and management of right iliac fossa pathology and remains difficult to identify preoperatively. Failure to recognize it can result in recurrent symptoms, missed pathology, intraoperative challenges, and medicolegal consequences. This report describes the case of a 45-year-old woman with history of a loculated peri-appendiceal abscess managed with percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics, subsequently found to have a duplicated appendix with mucocele identified after right hemicolectomy. CASE REPORT A 45-year-old woman presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and fever that began 2 months ago. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated ruptured appendicitis with a loculated peri-appendiceal abscess, successfully managed with percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics, resulting in clinical improvement. She re-presented 2 months later with recurrent abdominal pain. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed a dilated, firm appendiceal tip and a mass-like ileocecal inflammatory complex, raising suspicion of malignancy. Due to the distorted anatomy and inability to exclude an underlying neoplasm, a right hemicolectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed a Type B2 (Cave-Wallbridge) duplication of the appendix, one of which showed mucocele formation and features of resolving appendicitis with no evidence of malignancy. CONCLUSIONS Appendiceal duplication is classified according to the Cave-Wallbridge system and is rarely associated with appendiceal mucocele. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion and careful intraoperative assessment. Extended resection may be required when anatomy is distorted or malignancy cannot be excluded, to prevent missed pathology and recurrence.

title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
abstract: Introduction This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. Methods Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. Results The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

title: The Influence of Contralesional Brain Age Gradients on Chronic Stroke Aphasia Severity and Treatment Response.
abstract: The adult brain follows normative aging trajectories, yet stroke abruptly disrupts this process. Beyond the focal lesion, undamaged regions can deviate from expected aging due to diaschisis or pre-existing vulnerabilities, reflecting tissue health that may constrain recovery. Chronic post-stroke aphasia, a persistent language disorder, shows wide individual variability in severity and treatment response, and these differences are not fully captured by lesion characteristics or demographic factors. Further, prior imaging biomarkers have been difficult to scale because they rely on specialized acquisitions or nonstandardized analytical pipelines. Here, we used a standardized, lifespan-informed brain age model (volBrain) trained on large public datasets to quantify regional deviations from normative aging using only routine structural MRI (T1-weighted). In 188 individuals with chronic stroke (67 female, 121 male), regional aging deviations in the contralesional hemisphere explained aphasia severity beyond lesion volume, lesion location, and basic demographics. In a treated subgroup, baseline brain aging patterns also predicted language gains that persisted 6 months after therapy, indicating prognostic value. By characterizing how individual brains diverge from expected aging, this approach captures variation in tissue integrity that is relevant for both impairment and recovery. This provides a scalable framework that can be integrated across sites and studies, linking normative aging models with post-stroke prognostics and informing precision neurorehabilitation.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.
